goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Critical/security] app/models/topic_embed.rb:20 / app/views/embed/best.html.erb:24 — Imported feed/readability content is stored and cooked as raw_html, bypassing sanitization/markdown pipeline, then rendered with raw post.cooked, allowing script/event-handler markup in external feed content to become stored XSS executing on the Discourse origin inside the iframe; PollFeed feeds raw feed HTML straight in with no filtering

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces a raw-HTML rendering path for imported content with no sanitization: TopicEmbed.import creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true` (app/models/topic_embed.rb), and Post#cook returns `raw` when `cook_method == :raw_html`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline (app/models/post.rb). The embed view then renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb), meaning any `<script>` tags or inline event handlers present in external RSS/readability content will be stored and executed in the Discourse origin inside the iframe. Jobs::PollFeed also passes `i.content` straight through (after unescape/scrub) into TopicEmbed.import with no filtering (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb). This is a verifiable stored XSS risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/security] app/models/topic_embed.rb:20 — url is interpolated unescaped into HTML (#{url}), allowing a crafted embed URL (quotes, onerror=, etc.) to inject markup into the post body which is then rendered raw

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the `url` is directly interpolated into an HTML anchor (`"#{url}"`) and appended to `contents`. The only validation is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent quotes or other markup-breaking characters in the URL. This is then saved with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` for `:raw_html`, while the embed view renders it via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. Together, this makes crafted URLs capable of injecting arbitrary HTML/JS into the rendered post body.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/concurrency] app/models/topic_embed.rb:27-38 — Check-then-act race in import: two concurrent retrievals (web job + hourly PollFeed) can both see embed.blank? and both create a topic; the second TopicEmbed.create! violates the unique index and raises RecordNotUnique, leaking a created topic/post with no embed row and failing the job

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, it does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and then, if blank, creates a topic/post and finally `TopicEmbed.create!` (with a DB unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url`). Two concurrent calls with the same `url` can both observe `embed.blank?` and race into the create path; the second will hit the unique constraint and raise (no rescue/retry shown). Whether the topic/post leak depends on transaction boundaries inside `PostCreator`, but the check-then-act race and possible `RecordNotUnique` job failure are directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] lib/topic_retrieval.rb:26-33 (lib/topic_retriever.rb) — $redis.setnx followed by a separate $redis.expire is non-atomic; a crash between the two leaves the throttle key with no TTL, permanently blocking retrieval for that URL; use SET key val EX 60 NX

adjudication.rationale:
In the new `lib/topic_retriever.rb` method `retrieved_recently?`, the throttle is implemented as:

```ruby
if $redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")
  $redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)
  return false
end
```

Because `SETNX` and `EXPIRE` are separate commands, a process crash/network error between them can leave `retrieved_key` set with no TTL. That would make `retrieved_recently?` return `true` forever for that URL, effectively permanently blocking retrieval. Using atomic `SET retrieved_key 1 EX 60 NX` (or a Lua script) avoids this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/performance] lib/topic_retriever.rb:41-45 — When feed polling is enabled, every new embed URL synchronously runs the entire feed poll (Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})), re-fetching and re-parsing the whole feed inside the RetrieveTopic job; combined with open(...) having no timeout or size limit (poll_feed.rb:26, topic_embed.rb:41), a slow/huge remote can hang Sidekiq workers

adjudication.rationale: Verified in diff: TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve synchronously runs a full feed poll when SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled? (lib/topic_retriever.rb), calling Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) inside the RetrieveTopic job path. PollFeed uses open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb) and TopicEmbed.import_remote uses open(url).read (app/models/topic_embed.rb) with no explicit timeouts/size limits, so a slow/large remote can block Sidekiq worker threads and degrade availability. This is a real reliability/performance defect introduced by the new embed/feed retrieval flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/data] db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:4 — Modifying an already-applied migration to add force: true means environments that re-run it (or fresh setups replaying history against an existing DB) will drop and recreate top_topics, losing computed data; same pattern in the new create_topic_embeds migration

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration to `create_table :top_topics, force: true` (db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb). In Rails, `force: true` will drop an existing table before recreating it. While migrations normally run once, this introduces a concrete data-loss risk in cases where the migration is rerun (e.g., migrate:redo/rollback+reapply) or when running migration history against a DB that already has `top_topics`. The new migration `create_topic_embeds` also uses `force: true`, which would likewise drop `topic_embeds` if it already exists, making the concern diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] app/views/embed/best.html.erb:16 — post.user.small_avatar_url raises NoMethodError when the post's user has been deleted (user nil), breaking the whole embed page

adjudication.rationale: The new embed view does call `post.user.small_avatar_url` and `post.user.username` without a nil-guard, but the finding’s premise that `post.user` can be nil “when the user has been deleted” is not something the diff establishes. In this diff, embedded topics/posts are created via `PostCreator.new(user, ...)` using an existing user (`embed_by_username`), and there’s no change here showing users can be hard-deleted leaving orphaned `posts.user_id` (or that `post.user` becomes nil). Thus the claimed NoMethodError scenario isn’t verifiable from the PR diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:8 — The loading page reloads every 30s unconditionally and forever if the retrieval job failed; combined with discourse_expires_in 1.minute in EmbedController#best, proxies/CDNs may cache the loading page, delaying or preventing the content from ever appearing

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a loading template that always reloads the page every 30s via `setTimeout(... document.location.reload() ...)` (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb), with no stop condition or error handling if `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` never results in an embed being created (EmbedController#best). Additionally, `EmbedController#best` unconditionally calls `discourse_expires_in 1.minute`, so the loading response can be cached for up to a minute, meaning reloads may repeatedly hit a cached loading page even after the background job completes, delaying the real content.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/api] lib/tasks/disqus.thor:114-117 — The --category option was removed with no deprecation or error message, silently breaking existing invocations that pass -c; the import also now requires a live network fetch per thread (import_remote), so previously working offline/dry-run-style imports can fail mid-run

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the Thor CLI switch `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` and all logic that handled it (lib/tasks/disqus.thor), which is an API/CLI breaking change for existing invocations that used `-c/--category`. The diff also changes non-dry-run behavior to `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)`, which performs a live `open(url).read` network fetch per thread (app/models/topic_embed.rb), making imports dependent on network availability compared to the prior behavior that created a post from metadata only. However, it likely won’t be “silent”: Thor typically errors on unknown switches, and `--dry_run` still avoids the network call.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/security] app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:20 — e.data.height is used without validating it's a sane number; a compromised/malicious embedder can inject arbitrary strings into the iframe height attribute; cap/validate as a positive integer

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js the height is set from postMessage data, but messages are accepted only when `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) !== -1`, i.e., only from the Discourse iframe’s origin, not from the embedding parent (“malicious embedder” can’t satisfy this origin check). Also, assigning `iframe.height = e.data.height + "px"` sets a DOM attribute value, not HTML, so the claim of “inject arbitrary strings into the iframe height attribute” as a security issue is overstated given what the diff shows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:5 — No guard for a missing #discourse-comments element; the script throws a TypeError on publisher pages that include the snippet without the div

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, `comments` is set via `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` and then unconditionally used: `comments.appendChild(iframe);`. If the element is missing, `comments` will be `null` and `appendChild` will throw a `TypeError`. There is no guard or early return to handle this case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/performance] app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:16 — feed_key (conditional-fetch key based on feed modification) is defined but never used; the full feed is fetched and every item re-imported/checked hourly regardless of whether it changed

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, `feed_key` is defined (computes a redis key based on `SiteSetting.feed_polling_url`) but never referenced anywhere in `execute` or `poll_feed`. The job always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates `rss.items` hourly, relying on `TopicEmbed.import` to dedupe/update, so the feed is still fetched and all items are processed regardless of whether the feed changed. This is a concrete performance/efficiency concern grounded in the diff, not a correctness defect per se.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/doc_defect] config/site_settings.yml:354 / lib/topic_retriever.rb:14 — embeddable_host is compared against URI(...).host, so an admin entering a value with a scheme or path (http://example.com/) will silently never match; the setting description doesn't say "hostname only, no scheme"

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` the code compares `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` directly to `URI(@embed_url).host` (hostname only). Similarly `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` compares `URI(request.referer).host` to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. Since the setting is a free-form string (`config/site_settings.yml` adds `embeddable_host: ''`) and the description says only "Host that can embed..." (not "hostname only"), an admin entering `http://example.com/` would never match the parsed `.host` (`example.com`), causing embeds/retrieval to fail with invalid host behavior and no clear indication.
